label: The Testament of Benjamin Concerning a Pure Mind. — Translator and historical edition notes
context: The Testament of Benjamin Concerning a Pure Mind.

blocks.text: [^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-1]: The ordinary theory as to the meaning of Benjamin is comparatively late, and seems doubtful. The Targum Jerushalmi (on Gen. xxxv. 18 ), and the Breshith Rabba , § 82, make Benjamin and Benoni synonymous. Cf. Josephus, Antiq ., i. 21. 3; Cyril, Glaph. in Gen ., lib. iv. With the view mentioned in the text, cf. Arethas on Rev. vii. 8 (Cramer’s Catena , viii. 289).
[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-2]: This would seem to be the earliest instance of the application of the word ἀναμάρτητος to our Lord.
[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-3]: [How could any Christian more fully testify to the Nicene Faith? So the Gloria in Excelsis .]
[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-5]: For ἑπτακοσίοις ἔτεσιν the Ox. ms. reads simply ἑπτά .
[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-6]: This would seem to be the meaning of πρῶτος ναός .
[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-7]: [ Rev. xx. 5, 6 . See p. 25, note 4, supra .]

[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-8]: Gen. xlix. 27 . This passage, referring to St. Paul (who was of the tribe of Benjamin, Rom. xi. 1; Phil. iii. 5 ), is quoted by Tertullian, Adversus Marcionem , v. 1. [See vol. iii. p. 430, this series.]

[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-9]: Compare Scorpiace , cap. 13 [with reference to Gen. xxv. 34 and xxvii. 25 , vol. iii. p. 646, this series. Lardner adds Origen, Hom. in Ezech ., iv. tom. iii. p. 731; Theodoret, in Gen. Quæst ., cx. tom. i. p. 77; and Augustine, Serm ., 279 (and passim ), tom. v. ed. Benedict.].
[^testaments-twelve-patriarchs-iii-xiv-10]: [“Mel in ore, melos in aure, melodia in corde.”— St. Bernard .]
